chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

A man came to us in Mina and said, 'I did not catch up with the people at both standing places (al-Mawqifayn) together.' Abdullah ibn al-Mughira said to him, 'Then your Hajj is not valid.' He asked Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, but he did not answer him. So Isma'il entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and asked him about that. He said, 'If he catches up with Muzdalifah and stands at it before the sun moves (sets) on the Day of Nahr (Eid al-Adha), then he has caught up with the Hajj.'

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ الْحَجَّ: To have caught up with/validated the Hajj.
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: The two standing places, referring to Arafat and Muzdalifah.
key_terms.مُزْدَلِفَةَ: Muzdalifah, the plain between Mina and Arafat where pilgrims collect pebbles and pray.
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a valley near Mecca where pilgrims spend the days of Tashriq.
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Nahr (Sacrifice), referring to the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the standing at Arafat but reaches Muzdalifah before sunset on Eid al-Adha?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the standing at Arafat but reaches Muzdalifah before the sun sets on the Day of Nahr, affirming the validity of their Hajj. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the essential nature of the standing at Muzdalifah as a condition for Hajj completeness, distinguishing it from the Sunni view which often prioritizes Arafat alone. The narration underscores the flexibility in ritual timing, ensuring that pilgrims are not deprived of the reward due to minor delays in reaching the sacred sites.
